game.title: Food Myths & Kitchen Facts
game.description: Half of what people 'know' about cooking is wrong. Can you separate kitchen wisdom from kitchen myth?

questions.prompt: Searing a steak at high heat 'seals in the juices,' keeping the meat moist.
What does it mean to 'temper' chocolate when baking or candy-making?

options: Melt it very slowly in a double boiler to prevent burning
Heat and cool it to precise temperatures to form stable cocoa-butter crystals
Mix it with cream to create a smooth ganache
Add sugar gradually to balance bitterness

questions.prompt: Adding oil to your pasta water is an effective way to prevent the noodles from sticking together.
Scoville units are the standard measure of the ___ of chili peppers. (One word)
Which cooking oil has the highest smoke point, making it the best choice for high-heat searing?
Brown eggs are more nutritious than white eggs.
The technique of cooking vacuum-sealed food in a precisely temperature-controlled water bath is called ___ (a French term). (Two words)
Carrots were originally purple (and sometimes white or yellow) — the familiar orange variety was selectively cultivated in the Netherlands in the 17th century.
Umami is often called the fifth basic taste alongside sweet, sour, salty, and bitter. Which word best describes it?
Be honest — what's your real approach when a recipe says something takes 30 minutes?

options: I follow every step and time exactly as written
I read it once, then improvise based on vibes
I multiply the time by 1.5 and plan accordingly

questions.prompt: Which of the following foods are botanically classified as fruits? Select all that apply.
Which of these cooking methods use DRY heat — no water, liquid, or steam? Select all that apply.
Which of these kitchen myths did you believe before today? Be honest — select all that apply.

options: Adding oil to pasta water prevents sticking
Brown eggs are more nutritious than white eggs
You should always rinse raw chicken before cooking
